meta.note: Real data, aggregated from a personal end-of-day tracking log (2026-08-29 through 2026-09-02). Customer/account names anonymized. Only entries with a directly comparable AI-assisted vs. estimated-unassisted time are counted in the hours/multiplier stats below — entries marked 'not previously possible' or 'pending' are tracked separately rather than forced into a ratio.

scopeExpansion.title: Autonomous case tracking
scopeExpansion.before: Reviewing and escalating cases was a multi-day manual cycle per pass.
scopeExpansion.after: A fully autonomous tracker pulls, reviews, and alerts on cases daily — runs in minutes, no manual cycle required.

scopeExpansion.title: Data that was effectively unreachable
scopeExpansion.before: Key account identifiers were scattered across disconnected system fields, not reliably visible at all.
scopeExpansion.after: Sourced and reconciled in about an hour — not realistically doable manually in the time available.

scopeExpansion.title: This journal itself
scopeExpansion.before: No system existed for tracking personal output — it just didn't happen.
scopeExpansion.after: Designed and running within a day and a half, entirely in conversation, with no separate tool to learn.

scopeExpansion.title: Rush turnarounds
scopeExpansion.before: Consolidating account data into revenue-tied materials alone, under time pressure, wasn't realistic for one person.
scopeExpansion.after: Pulled, consolidated, and turned into finished slides in an afternoon.

sampleInterview.speaker: interviewer
sampleInterview.text: Walk me through today — what did you actually produce?

sampleInterview.speaker: user
sampleInterview.text: I got the manual trigger working for a reporting run that used to be fully manual — now it's just a 15-minute trigger.

sampleInterview.speaker: interviewer
sampleInterview.text: Got it, that's Automation / AI Tooling. Before this, how long did that reporting take start to finish?

sampleInterview.speaker: user
sampleInterview.text: Probably an hour, sometimes two, depending on how messy the source data was.

sampleInterview.speaker: interviewer
sampleInterview.text: Logged: 15 minutes assisted vs. roughly an hour-plus estimated. Anything else today?

sampleInterview.speaker: user
sampleInterview.text: Yeah, I also sourced some account identifiers that were scattered across a few disconnected system fields.

sampleInterview.speaker: interviewer
sampleInterview.text: That's data wrangling. Realistically, could you have pulled that together manually in the time you had?

sampleInterview.speaker: user
sampleInterview.text: Honestly, no — not without hours I didn't have.

sampleInterview.speaker: interviewer
sampleInterview.text: Logging that one as 'not previously possible' rather than a time comparison — that's its own category, and it matters as much as the hours saved.

roadmap.title: Manual end-of-day interview
roadmap.detail: Conversational capture, no live logging. Entries categorized and estimated together at day's end — currently running on real data since late August 2026.

roadmap.title: Calendar-aware interview
roadmap.detail: Once calendar/document connectors are available, the interview opens already aware of the day's meetings and blocked time, and asks about the gaps instead of starting cold.

roadmap.title: AI-populated calendar
roadmap.detail: The end goal: Claude drafts calendar tasks directly from observed work patterns, without being told what the tasks are first — flipping the interview from a data-capture step into a review-and-correct step.
